name: Greenwich
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Greenwich, CT 2026
seo_desc: Christmas events for kids in Greenwich, Connecticut for 2026: live reindeer, Santa's Holiday Village, the town tree lighting and a Polar Express movie night.
lede: Greenwich celebrates with live reindeer on North Street, a Santa village at the Old Greenwich civic center and a free tree lighting at Town Hall.
celebrates: The Town of Greenwich Parks and Recreation Department runs most of the town's family Christmas events and sells tickets through its recreation system. Its Annual Tree Lighting brings Santa, Rudolph and Frosty to Town Hall with candy canes, hot chocolate and cookies, and the town says attendance is free. Santa's Holiday Village fills the Cohen Eastern Greenwich Civic Center with crafts, games and a visit with Santa, and a holiday movie night follows at the Bendheim Western Greenwich Civic Center. Away from town buildings, the Greenwich Reindeer Festival at Sam Bridge Nursery & Greenhouses brings three live reindeer and Santa's Workshop to North Street from November 27 to December 24.
lastyear: We did not find a published recap of the 2025 town tree lighting, so this page relies on the host pages for 2026. The Greenwich Reindeer Festival says it is marking its 18th year in 2026 and calls the festival a tradition for thousands of families over the past 17 years, so it ran in 2025 too. The festival also says it donates a portion of every photo with Santa to Kids in Crisis, and it has done so for 18 years in a row.
facts: The Greenwich Reindeer Festival calls its home at Sam Bridge Nursery & Greenhouses the North Pole on North Street. On opening day, November 27, Santa arrives at noon in a Mercedes-Benz and cuts a ribbon with special guests. The festival lets families bring their dogs for photos with Santa, enters every photo in a raffle for a kids' electric car and lets kids vote to name the baby reindeer. The reindeer leave for the North Pole on the afternoon of December 23, and parking is free.
trains: We did not find a Christmas train ride in Greenwich itself. Our Connecticut guide at /blog/christmas-train-ride-connecticut lists the Christmas train rides across the state, and families who want a train day often look at the holiday train shows in nearby Fairfield and Stamford. Santa's Holiday Village and the town tree lighting are the town's own Santa events, and both take place at town buildings rather than on a railway.
traditions: The town lights its tree at Town Hall with Santa, Rudolph and Frosty, candy canes, hot chocolate, cookies and school performers.
Three live reindeer, photos with Santa and Santa's Workshop at Sam Bridge Nursery & Greenhouses from November 27 to December 24.
A ticketed morning of crafts, games, live entertainment and a visit with Santa at the Cohen Eastern Greenwich Civic Center.
A pajama party with a craft, cocoa and a showing of The Polar Express at the Bendheim Western Greenwich Civic Center.
The Reindeer Festival donates a portion of every photo with Santa to Kids in Crisis.
kidfact: At the Greenwich Reindeer Festival, kids can help name the baby reindeer, and Santa announces the winning name on December 24.
faq: How does Greenwich celebrate Christmas for kids?

The town holds a free Annual Tree Lighting at Town Hall with Santa, Rudolph and Frosty. Greenwich Parks and Recreation also runs Santa's Holiday Village and a Polar Express movie night, and the Greenwich Reindeer Festival brings live reindeer and Santa to North Street from November 27 to December 24.
Are there free Christmas events in Greenwich?

Yes. The Annual Tree Lighting at Town Hall is free and needs no tickets. The Reindeer Festival says no tickets or reservations are needed to walk up for photos with Santa, though the photos themselves have a cost, so check the festival site for prices.
Do I need tickets for Santa's Holiday Village in Greenwich?

Yes. The town says advance purchase is required, space is limited and tickets are not sold at the door. Tickets cost $20 per person, children under 1 are free, and each household can buy up to eight. Everyone needs a ticket, including infants, and tickets are Will Call only, so the buyer picks them up at check-in.
Can we bring our dog to see Santa in Greenwich?

Yes. The Greenwich Reindeer Festival says families can bring their dogs for photos with Santa any time the festival is open, and dogs get a free gift bag on weekdays. Check the festival site for the daily hours before you go.
Where do families park for the Greenwich Reindeer Festival?

The festival says parking is free at Sam Bridge Nursery & Greenhouses, 437 North Street, which it describes as just minutes from downtown Greenwich. Photos with Santa run Monday to Friday from noon to 6 pm, Saturday from 9 am to 6 pm, and Christmas Eve from 9 am to 3 pm.
